conferences.title: 1024 x MADMAPPER : History of the Interplay
conferences.description:
Depuis plus de 15 ans, 1024 Architecture et MadMapper évoluent côte à côte, à la croisée de l’art, de l’architecture, de la lumière, du son et de la technologie.

Cette conférence retrace l’histoire de cette relation : comment les projets artistiques ont stimulé le développement de nouveaux outils et comment ces outils ont, à leur tour, ouvert de nouvelles possibilités créatives.

Un voyage à travers les expérimentations, les projets, les échecs et les inventions, pour explorer le dialogue permanent entre la création artistique et la conception des outils qui la rendent possible.
conferences.description_en:
For over 15 years, 1024 architecture and MadMapper have evolved side by side, at the crossroads of art, architecture, light, sound and technology.

This talk traces the history of this interplay: how artistic projects have driven the development of new tools, and how these tools, in turn, have opened up new creative possibilities.

A journey through experiments, projects, failures and inventions — exploring the constant dialogue between making art and making the tools to make it.
conferences.speaker_bio:
1024 évolue à la croisée de l’art et de l’architecture, combinant pratiques spatiales, technologies numériques et création visuelle. En fusionnant les disciplines et les médias, le studio considère l’architecture et les espaces habités comme des structures en constante évolution. Les installations audiovisuelles deviennent alors des dispositifs pérennes, l’architecture se déconstruit en structures temporaires, la scénographie émerge comme une œuvre d’art et les performances multimédias se transforment en expériences immersives en temps réel. Des projets éphémères d’une nuit aux installations permanentes, 1024 Architecture crée des œuvres originales qui entrent en résonance avec leur environnement.

Après s’être rencontrés à l’École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture de Strasbourg, Pier Schneider et François Wunschel ont fondé 1024 Architecture en 2007. En 2014, ils ont été rejoints par Nico Merlin, architecte et compositeur, qui a intégré l’agence en tant qu’architecte, musicien et vidéaste. Depuis lors, le studio se consacre à la création et à la production d’installations audiovisuelles, fusionnant architecture et arts visuels dans un ensemble d’œuvres reconnu à l’international. Des objets de petite taille destinés aux expositions en intérieur aux installations monumentales dans l’espace public, les œuvres de 1024 se distinguent par leur approche unique de l’espace à travers la géométrie, la lumière, le son et le mouvement.
conferences.speaker_bio_en:
1024 operates at the crossroads of art and architecture, combining spatial practices, digital technologies, and visual creation. Merging disciplines and media, the studio considers architecture and inhabited spaces as evolving structures. Audiovisual installations then become perennial devices, architecture dismantles as temporary structures, scenography emerges as a work of art, and multimedia performances turn into real-time immersive experiences. From one-night projects to permanent installations, 1024 architecture creates original works that resonate within their environment. 

After meeting at the École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture de Strasbourg, Pier Schneider and François Wunschel founded 1024 Architecture in 2007. In 2014, they were joined by Nico Merlin, an architect, and composer who integrated the agency as an architect, musician, and video maker. Since then, the studio has focused on creating and producing audiovisual installations, fusing architecture and the visual arts in an internationally recognized body of work. From small-scale objects intended for indoor exhibitions to monumental installations in the public space, what distinguishes 1024 works is their unique approach to space through the tools of geometry, light, sound, and movement.

by_night_events.description:
Pour ses 15 ans, le KIKK Festival s'associe à MUTEK et Les Orgues De Saint-Loup en invitant Sarah Davachi, figure majeure de la scène alternative de l'orgue. 
Ce concert n’est pas inclus dans les pass KIKK – un billet séparé est nécessaire !

Sarah Davachi (née en 1987 au Canada) est une compositrice et interprète dont le travail s’intéresse aux subtilités de l’espace timbral et temporel, utilisant des durées étendues et des systèmes d’accordage alternatifs afin de mettre en évidence les variations progressives de texture, la complexité des harmoniques, la résonance harmonique, l’intonation et les phénomènes psychoacoustiques. Ses compositions couvrent des formats solo, pour ensemble de chambre et acousmatiques, intégrant un large éventail d’instruments acoustiques et électroniques. Également nourri par les structures minimalistes et de longue durée, les concepts de musique ancienne liés aux relations intervalliques et à l’affect, ainsi que par les pratiques de production expérimentales propres à l’environnement du studio, son univers sonore offre une expérience intime et patiente qui reconfigure notre perception du familier et du lointain.

Parallèlement à ses enregistrements salués par la critique, Davachi a effectué de nombreuses tournées et performances ; son travail a été présenté internationalement par le Southbank Centre (Londres), le Barbican Centre (Londres), Radio France (Paris), l’Elbphilharmonie (Hambourg), Organ Reframed (Londres), le Museum of Modern Art (New York), le Getty Museum (Los Angeles), l’Academy Museum (Los Angeles), le Broad Museum (Los Angeles), le Walt Disney Concert Hall (Los Angeles), le Museo Reina Sofía (Madrid), Orgelpark (Amsterdam), le temple Honen-in (Kyoto), Muziekgebouw (Amsterdam), l’église Saint-Eustache (Paris), St Martin-in-the-Fields (Londres), l’église Temppeliaukio (Helsinki), Grace Cathedral (San Francisco), la Chiesa di San Luigi dei Francesi (Rome), l’église du Gesù (Montréal), Carriageworks (Sydney) et le Teatro Cultural Artística (São Paulo), entre autres. Ses œuvres pour ensemble de chambre ont été commandées et interprétées par le Los Angeles Philharmonic, le Brussels Philharmonic, le London Contemporary Orchestra, Microtub, le Quatuor Bozzini, le Harmonic Space Orchestra, Apartment House, Ghost Ensemble, Wild Up, Yarn/Wire, Chamber Choir Ireland, le BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra, Contemporaneous Ensemble, GBSR Duo, Diapason, Cello Octet Amsterdam et le Concours international d’orgue du Canada. Parmi ses principales distinctions figurent le Lion d’argent en 2026, décerné par La Biennale di Venezia, ainsi qu’un Libera Award en 2023, décerné par l’American Association of Independent Music. En 2020, elle a fondé Late Music, un label au sein de la division des labels partenaires de Warp Records, qui constitue désormais un foyer permanent pour ses albums et ses enregistrements.

Pendant plus d’une décennie, Davachi a eu l’occasion unique de travailler pour le National Music Centre au Canada en tant que chercheuse et interprète de sa collection d’instruments à clavier acoustiques et électroniques. Elle est titulaire d’un master en musique électronique du Mills College et d’un doctorat en musicologie de l’UCLA (avec une thèse consacrée au timbre, à la phénoménologie et à l’organologie critique), et est basée à Los Angeles, en Californie, aux États-Unis.

Sarah Davachi donnera un concert solo d'orgue au cours duquel elle interprétera de nouvelles œuvres tirées de son prochain album, The Will of Tongues, qui sortira chez Late Music le 28 août, ainsi que plusieurs morceaux de son précédent album, The Head as Form'd in the Crier's Choir (2024).

Cette performance est co-présenté par Les Orgues de Saint-Loup, MUTEK, avec le soutien financier du Conseil des arts du Canada

For its 15th anniversary, KIKK Festival joins forces with MUTEK and Les Orgues de Saint-Loup to welcome Sarah Davachi, a leading figure in the alternative organ scene.  
This concert is not included in KIKK passes – separate ticket required.

Sarah Davachi (b. 1987, Canada) is a composer and performer whose work is concerned with the close intricacies of timbral and temporal space, utilizing extended durations and alternate tuning systems to underscore gradual variations in texture, overtone complexity, harmonic resonance, intonation, and psychoacoustic phenomena.  Her compositions span solo, chamber ensemble, and acousmatic formats, incorporating a wide range of both acoustic and electronic instrumentation.  Similarly informed by minimalist and longform structures, early music concepts of intervallic relation and affect, as well as experimental production practices of the studio environment, in her sound is an intimate and patient experience that reconfigures perceptions of the familiar and the distant.

​Alongside her acclaimed recordings, Davachi has toured and performed extensively; her work has been presented internationally by Southbank Centre (London), Barbican Centre (London), Radio France (Paris), Elbphilharmonie (Hamburg), Organ Reframed (London), The Museum of Modern Art (New York), The Getty Museum (Los Angeles), The Academy Museum (Los Angeles), The Broad Museum (Los Angeles), Walt Disney Concert Hall (Los Angeles), Museo Reina Sofía (Madrid), Orgelpark (Amsterdam), Honen-in Temple (Kyoto), Muziekgebouw (Amsterdam), Église Saint-Eustache (Paris), St Martin-in-the-Fields (London), Temppeliaukio Church (Helsinki), Grace Cathedral (San Francisco), Chiesa di San Luigi dei Francesi (Rome), Église du Gesù (Montréal), Carriageworks (Sydney), and Teatro Cultural Artística (São Paulo), among others.  Her chamber ensemble work has been commissioned and performed by the Los Angeles Philharmonic, the Brussels Philharmonic, the London Contemporary Orchestra, Microtub, Quatuor Bozzini, Harmonic Space Orchestra, Apartment House, Ghost Ensemble, Wild Up, Yarn/Wire, Chamber Choir Ireland, the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra, Contemporaneous Ensemble, GBSR Duo, Diapason, Cello Octet Amsterdam, and the Canadian International Organ Competition.  Major recognitions include the Silver Lion award in 2026, given by La Biennale di Venezia, and a Libera award in 2023, given by the American Association of Independent Music.  In 2020 she founded Late Music, an imprint within the partner labels division of Warp Records, which serves as a permanent home for her albums and recordings.

For over a decade, Davachi had the unique opportunity to work for the National Music Centre in Canada as a researcher and interpreter of their collection of acoustic and electronic keyboard instruments.  She holds a master's degree in electronic music from Mills College and a doctoral degree in musicology from UCLA (with a dissertation on timbre, phenomenology, and critical organology), and is based in Los Angeles, California, USA.

Sarah Davachi will present a solo organ concert of new works from her forthcoming album, The Will of Tongues, which was released on Late Music on August 28, alongside several pieces from her previous album, The Head as Form'd in the Crier's Choir (2024).  

This performance is co-presented by Les Orgues de Saint-Loup, MUTEK, with the financial support of the Canada Council for the Arts

20:30 - Papyluc Soundsystem (DJ set)

Le duo bruxellois Papyluc Soundsystem propose des sets énergiques et rythmés, ancrés dans la house, l’indie dance et les genres apparentés. Attendez-vous à des rythmes organiques, des touches acid et une multitude de pépites inattendues, le tout lié par un instinct de danseur hors pair. Depuis 2019, Maxime et Nicolas concoctent des sets conçus pour créer une dynamique, rassembler les gens et faire bouger les corps.

22:00 - LES EMPIRES - Guillaume Coutu-Dumont et Line Katcho (performance)

Véritable odyssée surréaliste, LES EMPIRES est une œuvre aux sonorités synthétiques prononcées, inspirée par la science-fiction et la mythologie. Elle dépeint la nature cyclique du pouvoir, de la décadence et de la renaissance à travers le prisme d’empires imaginaires qui n’ont jamais existé.

Inspiré par les vétérans du krautrock Manuel Göttsching et Tangerine Dream, et plus récemment par des artistes tels qu’Alessandro Cortini ou Caterina Barbieri, Guillaume Coutu-Dumont compose des morceaux rétrofuturistes empreints de chaleur et d’imperfections, caractéristiques des sons synthétiques ambiants d’une autre époque. Des percussions douces et des mélodies répétitives créent une atmosphère hypnotique et nostalgique qui évoque une époque qui n’a peut-être jamais existé.

Mêlant visuels abstraits, symbolisme et fils narratifs fragmentés, Line Katcho évoque un mirage changeant de structures de pouvoir qui s’élèvent et s’effondrent en boucles éternelles, faisant écho à des passés oubliés et à des futurs inventés. Le temps se courbe, l’histoire s’estompe, et le spectateur se retrouve à naviguer parmi les vestiges psychologiques de l’ambition et de l’entropie.

Line Katcho est une compositrice et artiste des nouveaux médias montréalaise qui travaille à la croisée du son et de l’image. À travers la performance audiovisuelle, le cinéma, la réalité virtuelle et le mapping vidéo, elle crée des expériences viscérales et cinématographiques, fusionnant l’abstraction et la narration, l’expérimentation et la tradition, ainsi que l’émotion brute et la précision formelle. Son œuvre est sensorielle, cathartique et indéniablement la sienne.

Formé aux percussions classiques et latines ainsi qu’à la composition électroacoustique, Guillaume Coutu Dumont est une figure incontournable de la scène électronique montréalaise depuis le début des années 2000. Sous son pseudonyme solo Guillaume & The Coutu Dumonts, il a fusionné la house, le jazz, le gospel et l’afrobeat, ce qui l’a conduit à effectuer plus d’une décennie de tournées dans plus de 45 pays. Ses œuvres récentes explorent un style ambient teinté de nostalgie et d’analogique, alliant répétitions hypnotiques, chaleur mélodique et rythme instinctif.

Ce spectacle est coprésenté par MUTEK, avec le soutien financier du Conseil des Arts du Canada et du Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec.


23:00 - Elsewhere in India (performance)

Elsewhere in India » est une série d’œuvres qui explore le patrimoine culturel, les technologies numériques et des futurs hypothétiques à travers le cinéma, des expériences interactives, des jeux vidéo et la sculpture, créées par les artistes Murthovic et Thiruda.

Elsewhere in India » imagine un avenir façonné par l’amnésie culturelle. Se déroulant en 2079 après J.-C., le récit s’articule autour de Meenakshi, un « cyborg culturel » conçu pour préserver le patrimoine sud-asiatique et promouvoir l’innovation multiculturelle. L’expérience associe des supports numériques de pointe — jeux vidéo en 3D, art généré par l’IA, danse capturée par motion capture et images d’archives — afin d’explorer comment le patrimoine, la science et la société s’entremêlent dans un monde indo-futuriste imaginaire. Il en résulte un voyage à la fois ludique et stimulant à travers l’avenir spéculatif de l’Inde, souligné par une musique de danse électro-classique émergente.


23:55 - Deena Abdelwahed (DJ set)

Deena Abdelwahed est une DJ et productrice tunisienne de musique électronique, basée entre la France et la Tunisie. Elle est reconnue pour sa manière singulière de mêler influences musicales arabes et électroniques contemporaines, dans une approche ancrée dans la Global Club Music. Depuis 2017, elle sort ses projets sur le label InFiné, avec plusieurs EP, deux albums dont Jbal Rrsas paru en 2023, ainsi que de nombreux remixes et collaborations. En DJ set comme en live, elle fait voyager son univers sonore sur les scènes du monde entier.


23:55 - Mike Latona aka Los Hermanos 

Graphiste de formation, Mike Latona aka Los Hermanos se passionne pour la peinture et la vidéo. Autodidacte, il allie rapidement les trois techniques auxquels s’ajoutent d’innombrables expériences plastiques.

Membre actif du collectif Détritu qui réalise un fanzine et des expositions dans un esprit trash, c’est aussi un artiste engagé impliqué dans les associations culturelles de la Ville de Liège. Il œuvre à une intégration de l’art dans le réel de façon innovante en utilisant des supports souvent inattendus, son leitmotiv étant l’expérimentation de nouveaux médias. Mixe de technique, son travail est coloré, souple et dynamique ; imprégné d’un sens positif, d’humour, d’esprit critique, de cohérence, privilégiant les collaborations entre artiste.

A ces activités s’allie le VJ’ing où il utilise l’image comme vecteur de son travail de graphiste pour toucher un autre public, il s’exporte à Berlin, Barcelone, Rome, …

Mike créé un univers que l’on retrouve sur des tee-shirts, stickers, dans des décorations de magasins, sur tout objet du quotidien, dans des sites web, sur des affiches, …

Univers qui véhicule un art se voulant communiquant, présent là où on ne l’attend pas, il s’inscrit dans le courant Street-Art. Mike Latona est un plasticien qui possède la volonté pour relever les défis, toujours aller plus loin dans la quête artistique, par le biais de rencontres, de voyages et ne se complait pas dans un domaine maîtrisé. C’est un artiste poussé par la recherche de nouveauté, un artiste qui ne s’arrête pas de chercher quand il a trouvé, restant toujours intègre à ses convictions.


01:30- Closing

20:30 - Papyluc Soundsystem (DJ set)

Brussels-based duo Papyluc Soundsystem delivers energetic, groove-driven sets rooted in house, indie dance and related sounds. Expect organic rhythms, acid touches, and plenty of unexpected gems, all held together by a strong dancefloor instinct. Since 2019, Maxime and Nicolas have been crafting sets designed to build momentum, connect people and keep bodies moving.


22:00 - LES EMPIRES - Guillaume Coutu-Dumont et Line Katcho (performance)

In a surreal odyssey, LES EMPIRES is a synth-heavy piece inspired by science-fiction and mythology. It depicts the cyclical nature of power, decay, and rebirth through the lens of imaginary empires that never existed.

Inspired by Krautrock veterans Manuel Göttsching and Tangerine Dream and more recently by artists like Alessandro Cortini or Caterina Barbieri, Guillaume Coutu-Dumont composes retro-futuristic pieces full of warmth and imperfections, typical of the ambient synthetic sounds of another era. Soft percussion and repetitive melodies create a hypnotic and nostalgic atmosphere reminiscent of an age that may never have existed.

Merging abstract visuals, symbolism and fractured narrative threads, Line Katcho conjures a shifting mirage of power structures rising and crumbling in eternal loops, echoing forgotten pasts and fabricated futures. Time bends, history blurs, and the viewer is left navigating the psychological remains of ambition and entropy.

Line Katcho is a Montreal composer and new media artist working at the intersection of sound and image. Across AV performance, film, virtual reality, and projection mapping, she creates visceral and cinematic experiences, fusing abstraction with narrative, experimentation with tradition, and raw affect with formal precision. Her work is sensory, cathartic, and unmistakably her own.

Trained in classical and Latin percussion and electroacoustic composition, Guillaume Coutu Dumont has been a central figure in Montréal’s electronic scene since the early 2000s. His solo alias Guillaume & The Coutu Dumonts fused house, jazz, gospel, and afrobeat, leading to over a decade of touring across more than 45 countries. His recent work explores a nostalgic, analog-infused ambient style, balancing hypnotic repetition, melodic warmth, and instinctive rhythm.

This performance is co-presented by MUTEK, with the financial support of the Canada Council for the Arts and the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec.


23:00 - Elsewhere in India (performance)

Elsewhere in India is a body of work that explores cultural heritage, digital technology, and speculative futures through film, interactive experiences, video games, and sculpture, created by artists Murthovic and Thiruda.

Elsewhere in India envisions a future shaped by cultural amnesia. Set in 2079 AD, the narrative is anchored by Meenakshi, a ‘cultural cyborg’ designed to safeguard South Asian heritage and promote multicultural innovation. The experience fuses cutting-edge digital mediums—3D video games, AI art, motion-captured dance, and archival footage—to explore how heritage, science, and society intertwine in an imagined Indo-futurist world. The result is a playful yet thought-provoking journey through India's speculative future, underscored by emergent electro-classical dance music.


23:55 - Deena Abdelwahed (DJ set)

Deena Abdelwahed is a Tunisian electronic music DJ and producer based between France and Tunisia. She is known for her unique way of blending Arab and contemporary electronic musical influences, in a style rooted in Global Club Music. Since 2017, she has been releasing her work on the InFiné label, including several EPs, two albums, one of which is Jbal Rrsas, released in 2023, as well as numerous remixes and collaborations. Whether in DJ sets or live performances, she brings her soundscapes to stages around the world.

23:55 - Mike Latona, aka Los Hermanos

Trained as a graphic designer, Mike Latona, aka Los Hermanos, has a passion for painting and video. Self-taught in these disciplines, he quickly began combining all three techniques, alongside countless experiments in the visual arts.

An active member of the Détritu collective, which produces a fanzine and exhibitions with a trash aesthetic, he is also a committed artist involved in cultural associations in the City of Liège. He works to bring art into everyday reality in innovative ways, often using unexpected media, with experimentation as his guiding principle. Blending techniques, his work is colourful, fluid and dynamic, infused with a positive outlook, humour, critical thinking and coherence, with an emphasis on collaborations between artists.

Alongside these activities, he also works as a VJ, using imagery to bring his graphic design work to a different audience, taking him to Berlin, Barcelona, Rome and beyond.

Mike creates a universe that appears on T-shirts, stickers, in shop interiors, on everyday objects, websites, posters and more.

Conveying an art that seeks to communicate and appearing where least expected, this universe is rooted in Street Art. Mike Latona is a visual artist determined to take on challenges and continually push his artistic exploration further through encounters and travel, never settling into a field he has already mastered. Driven by the search for new ideas, he is an artist who does not stop searching once he has found something, always remaining true to his convictions.

21:30 - 1 DROP 1000 YEARS - Martin Messier (Performance)

Les scientifiques s’accordent à dire qu’une goutte d’eau parcourt le globe en moins de 1 000 ans. Cette goutte sculpte notre monde : elle transporte nutriments, chaleur et organismes vivants, tout en régulant le climat et les écosystèmes de notre planète. Elle contribue au processus fondamental pour l’équilibre du vivant.

S’appuyant sur les données du Global Conveyor Belt, ce vaste courant océanique qui orchestre le brassage des eaux des cinq océans et redistribue la chaleur à l’échelle mondiale, Martin Messier souligne le rôle fondamental de l’eau comme substance vitale. Pourtant, depuis deux siècles, l’action humaine ébranle cet équilibre fragile : le ralentissement progressif de ce courant océanique pourrait provoquer un bouleversement climatique majeur, menaçant l’ensemble de la chaîne du vivant.

Dans cette performance hypnotique, l’artiste explore les tensions entre les courants globaux, moteurs de l’équilibre planétaire, et les courants intimes qui résonnent en chacun de nous. Quinze dispositifs suspendus, véritables sculptures cinétiques, orchestrent en temps réel le flux des particules d’eau, matérialisant les dynamiques océaniques. Les motifs générés, nourris par des données telles que la température et la salinité de l’océan Pacifique, s’entrelacent dans une chorégraphie visuelle et sonore. 1 drop 1000 years se dévoile ainsi comme un ballet magistral et poétique, traduisant la fragilité des écosystèmes et l’harmonie délicate qui lie toutes choses sur Terre.

Figure incontournable de la scène artistique québécoise et internationale, Martin Messier orchestre un dialogue entre son, lumière et mouvements. Son art de la mise en scène et son aptitude à combiner les technologies aux éléments naturels (eau, fumée, ondes, électricité…) l'ont conduit à développer un corpus sur notre perception des phénomènes physiques. Il explore leurs manifestations - des plus imperceptibles aux plus monumentales - par le biais de dispositifs extraordinaires. Ses performances et installations oscillent entre ordre et chaos, instaurent une tension contemplative conviant le public à vivre une expérience synesthésique, parfois proche du spirituel.

Cette performance est co-présenté par MUTEK, avec le soutien financier du Conseil des arts du Canada et du Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec.


22:00 - Dalidark b2b Joe d'Absynth (Dj set)

Récemment, animée par une passion dévorante pour la musique électronique, Dalidark (alias Eléonore) a enfin osé sortir de l’ombre pour se retrouver sous les feux de la rampe.
L’artiste aime décrire ses sets comme des « accidents artistiques prémédités » : soigneusement orchestrés, mais empreints d’instinct et d’émotion.
Ils mêlent des beats industriels percutants à des textures de synthé mélancoliques, où la dualité règne en maître : des rythmes EBM hypnotiques et disco sombres côtoient la séduction langoureuse de l’Italo disco, le tout enveloppé dans une lueur synthwave crépusculaire.

Joe d’Absynth (alias Greg) est membre du collectif Cosmic, qui organise des soirées du même nom à Liège, en Belgique.
Co-animateur du podcast francophone Cosmic, L’émission (https://poscast.cosmiverse.be)
Il a forgé sa culture musicale principalement à travers le rock classique et le jazz. Il s’est tourné vers la techno il y a une dizaine d’années, redécouvrant les sons New Wave et New Beat qui avaient inconsciemment marqué son oreille durant son enfance. Ses styles préférés vont de la synth-pop française à la techno minimale, en passant par la new wave, la dark wave, la cold wave, le post-punk et l’italo-disco.
Il est passionné par la scène dark disco et par des artistes tels que Curses, Local Suicide, Theus Mago, Damon Jee ou Moderna, parmi tant d’autres.

Éléonore et Greg (Dalidark & Joe d'Absynth) se produiront pour la première fois ensemble dans un set en duo. Ils vous emmèneront dans un voyage groovy oscillant entre italo et dark disco, synthwave et EBM. Attendez-vous à des sons de synthés des années 80 ainsi qu'à une musique de club aux accents berlinois.


01:30 - Closing
by_night_events.description_en:
21:30 - 1 DROP 1000 YEARS - Martin Messier (Performance)

Scientists agree that a drop of water travels the globe in less than 1,000 years. This drop shapes our world: it transports nutrients, heat and living organisms, while regulating our planet's climate and ecosystems. It contributes to the fundamental process of life's equilibrium.

Drawing on data from the Global Conveyor Belt, the vast ocean current that orchestrates the mixing of water from the five oceans and redistributes heat on a global scale, Martin Messier underlines the fundamental role of water as a vital substance. Yet, over the past two centuries, human action has been shaking this fragile balance: the gradual slowing of this ocean current could trigger a major climatic upheaval, threatening the entire chain of life.

In this hypnotic performance, the artist explores the tensions between the global currents that drive planetary equilibrium, and the intimate currents that resonate within each of us. Fifteen suspended devices, veritable kinetic sculptures, orchestrate the flow of water particles in real time, materializing oceanic dynamics. The patterns generated, fed by data such as the temperature and salinity of the Pacific Ocean, intertwine in a visual and sonic choreography. 1 drop 1000 years reveals itself as a masterful, poetic ballet, conveying the fragility of ecosystems and the delicate harmony that binds all things on Earth.

A key figure on the Quebec and international art scenes, Martin Messier orchestrates a dialogue between sound, light and movement. His art of staging and his ability to combine technologies with natural elements (water, smoke, waves, electricity...) have led him to develop a body of work on our perception of physical phenomena. He explores their manifestations - from the most imperceptible to the most monumental - through extraordinary devices. His performances and installations oscillate between order and chaos, creating a contemplative tension that invites the audience into a synesthetic experience, sometimes close to the spiritual.

This performance is co-presented by MUTEK, with the financial support of the Canada Council for the Arts and the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec


22:00 - Dalidark b2b Joe d'Absynth (Dj set)

Recently, driven by a burning passion for electronic music, Dalidark (aka Eléonore) has finally dared to step out of the shadows and into the spotlight.
The artist likes to describe her sets as "premeditated artistic accidents"—carefully curated, yet charged with instinct and emotion.
They fuse pounding industrial beats with melancholic synth textures, where duality is queen: hypnotic EBM and dark disco rhythms meet the languid seduction of Italo disco, all wrapped in a dusky synthwave glow.

Joe d'Absynth (aka Greg) is a member of the Cosmic collective which throws the equally named parties, in Liège, Belgium.
Co-host of the french speaking podcast Cosmic, L'émission (https://poscast.cosmiverse.be)
He forged his musical culture mainly with classic rock and jazz. Came to techno a decade ago, rediscovering New Wave and New Beat sounds that unconsciously marked his ear during childhood. Favorite styles extends from french SynthPop to minimal techno through new/dark/cold wave, post-punk and Italo-disco.
In love with the Dark Disco scene and artists as Curses, Local Suicide, Theus Mago, Damon Jee or Moderna among many others.

Éléonore and Greg (Dalidark & Joe d'Absynth) will perform their first back to back set together. They'll take in a groovy journey oscillating between italo and dark disco, synthwave and EBM. You can expect 80's synths sounds as well as more Berlin infused club music

by_night_events.description:
Azo est une DJ, artiste de scène et productrice franco-brésilienne basée à Bruxelles. Résidente sur Kiosk Radio et cofondatrice du Queer Future Club et du Queer Mess Festival, elle s’est rapidement imposée comme une figure montante de la scène internationale de la musique électronique.

Pianiste de formation classique et ingénieure du son, elle passe avec aisance des sets de DJ aux performances live. Azo évolue entre l’électro, la house, la techno et les breaks, inspirée par la culture rave britannique et l’héritage intemporel de la techno de Détroit. Ses sets sont énergiques et émouvants, captivant le public du début à la fin.

En tant que productrice, elle combine des synthétiseurs nostalgiques, des mélodies entraînantes et des rythmes endiablés pour créer un son unique. À l’aide de matériel analogique d’origine, notamment un Roland TB-303 original, elle façonne un son analogique caractéristique, conçu pour la piste de danse.

Au fil des ans, elle s’est produite dans certains des clubs et festivals les plus prestigieux au monde, notamment Tomorrowland (BE), le Dour Festival (BE), Nuits Sonores (FR), Sónar Off (ES), Positive Education (FR), Astropolis (FR), Watergate (DE), Concrete (FR), le Rex Club (FR), Horst (BE), le Listen Festival (BE), le C12 (BE), le Fuse (BE), le Paradise City Festival (BE), le Renate (DE), le Carpet Shop (UK), le KM25 (DE), ainsi que sur Rinse France, The Lot Radio (NYC) et N10.AS (CA).

panels.title: From Event to Experience
panels.description:
Un grand événement live ne se résume plus à ce qui se passe sur scène.

Les festivals, expositions et formats de divertissement deviennent de plus en plus des univers à part entière, où l’art, l’architecture, la scénographie, le storytelling, la technologie, le son et les interactions sociales façonnent l’expérience autant que le programme lui-même.

Mais que faut-il réellement pour transformer un événement en une expérience ?

Réunissant les perspectives de Moment Factory, Balloon Museum et Public Art Company / Coachella, cette conversation explore la manière dont des expériences mémorables sont imaginées, curatées et produites à grande échelle. Comment concevoir un univers dans lequel les gens ont envie d’entrer ? Comment trouver l’équilibre entre spectacle et sens ? Comment l’espace physique, la technologie et l’art façonnent-ils la manière dont les publics se connectent ? Et alors que les attentes ne cessent de croître, qu’est-ce qui rendra les expériences live de demain véritablement inoubliables ?

Modérée par Sandra Mekler de Fever, cette conversation réunit des créateur·rices travaillant sur certains des formats live, culturels et expérientiels les plus ambitieux d’aujourd’hui.
panels.description_en:
A great live event is no longer just about what happens on stage.

Festivals, exhibitions and entertainment formats are increasingly becoming worlds of their own, where art, architecture, scenography, storytelling, technology, sound and social interaction shape the experience as much as the programme itself.

But what does it actually take to turn an event into an experience?

Bringing together perspectives from Moment Factory, Balloon Museum and Public Art Company / Coachella, this conversation explores how memorable experiences are conceived, curated and produced at scale. How do you design a world people want to enter? How do you balance spectacle with meaning? How do physical space, technology and art shape the way audiences connect? And as expectations keep rising, what will make tomorrow’s live experiences truly unforgettable?

Moderated by Sandra Mekler from Fever, the conversation brings together creators working across some of today’s most ambitious live, cultural and experiential formats.

moderator.description: Sandra Mekler est Director of Institutional Relations & Communications chez Fever, la plateforme mondiale de découverte d’expériences de divertissement live et producteur à l’origine d’expériences allant de formats culturels et immersifs à de grands projets de divertissement internationaux. Travaillant à la croisée des secteurs public et privé, Sandra développe des partenariats et des échanges autour de l’économie de l’expérience, en pleine croissance, en créant des liens entre organisations culturelles, entreprises du divertissement, villes et industries créatives.
moderator.description_en: Sandra Mekler is Director of Institutional Relations & Communications at Fever, the global live-entertainment discovery platform and producer behind experiences ranging from cultural and immersive formats to major international entertainment projects. Working at the intersection of the public and private sectors, Sandra develops partnerships and conversations around the rapidly growing experience economy, connecting cultural organisations, entertainment companies, cities and creative industries.

speakers.description: Catherine Turp est Senior Director of Creation chez Moment Factory, le studio international de divertissement multimédia à l’origine d’expériences à grande échelle, d’installations publiques et de productions live à travers le monde. Travaillant à la croisée de l’art, de la technologie et du design, elle dirige des équipes multidisciplinaires dans la création d’environnements immersifs qui utilisent la technologie non pas comme une fin en soi, mais comme un outil au service de l’émotion, de la connexion et de l’expérience collective.
speakers.description_en: Catherine Turp is Senior Director of Creation at Moment Factory, the international multimedia entertainment studio behind large-scale experiences, public installations and live productions around the world. Working at the intersection of art, technology and design, she leads multidisciplinary teams in creating immersive environments that use technology not as an end in itself, but as a tool for emotion, connection and collective experience.

speakers.description: Francesco Dobrovich est directeur créatif, curateur et stratège culturel, travaillant à la croisée de l’art, des villes et de la culture immersive. En tant que Head of Art & Curation chez Lux Entertainment, il est étroitement impliqué dans le développement de Balloon Museum, un format international d’art expérientiel qui place les publics au cœur d’installations monumentales et interactives. Au cours des quinze dernières années, il a fondé et développé des plateformes culturelles telles qu’Outdoor Festival, Videocittà et Balloon Museum, explorant la manière dont l’art contemporain peut dépasser les espaces d’exposition traditionnels pour devenir une expérience à grande échelle, accessible et partagée.
speakers.description_en: Francesco Dobrovich is a creative director, curator and cultural strategist working at the intersection of art, cities and immersive culture. As Head of Art & Curation at Lux Entertainment, he is closely involved in the development of Balloon Museum, the international experiential art format that places audiences at the centre of monumental, interactive installations. Over the past fifteen years, he has founded and developed cultural platforms including Outdoor Festival, Videocittà and Balloon Museum, exploring how contemporary art can move beyond traditional exhibition spaces and become a large-scale, accessible and shared experience.

speakers.description: Raffi Lehrer est le fondateur de Public Art Company, un studio basé à Los Angeles qui assure le commissariat, la direction artistique et la production d’œuvres d’art public à grande échelle. Au cours de la dernière décennie, il a dirigé le volet curatorial du Coachella Art Program, commandant des œuvres monumentales à des artistes tels que Francis Kéré, Edoardo Tresoldi, Sabine Marcelis et Phillip K Smith III pour un public de plus de 125 000 personnes par week-end. Son travail explore la manière dont l’art à grande échelle peut transformer les festivals et les espaces publics en expériences mémorables, plusieurs commandes réalisées pour Coachella étant ensuite devenues des œuvres permanentes à travers la vallée de Coachella.
speakers.description_en: Raffi Lehrer is the founder of Public Art Company, a Los Angeles studio curating, art directing and producing large-scale public art. For the past decade, he has led the curatorial side of the Coachella Art Program, commissioning monumental works by artists including Francis Kéré, Edoardo Tresoldi, Sabine Marcelis and Phillip K Smith III for audiences of over 125,000 people per weekend. His work explores how large-scale art can transform festivals and public spaces into memorable experiences, with several Coachella commissions later becoming permanent artworks across the Coachella Valley.

panels.title: Reimagine/ Reinventing the City
panels.description_en:
Rethinking the city through culture: four trajectories, four different scales of intervention. From Oulu, where a European Capital of Culture is reshaping the identity of a mid-sized city over the long term, to Differdange, where a former steel site has become a creative hub; from Canary Wharf's business district, where public art finds its way into a territory built for commerce, to the large-scale, temporary spectacles designed by Filmmaster to transform how an entire city is seen, if only for the duration of an event.
Four complementary approaches, cultural policy, industrial reconversion, public art in private territory, and large-scale urban spectacle, to explore what makes a city feel alive today: duration, use, image, or the moment itself.

moderator.description_en: Emmanuel Angeli is a cultural project and events professional at Brussels Major Events, with a strong background in urban arts, public space and socio-cultural projects, working to promote Brussels’ creative and cultural industries through inclusive and innovative events.

speakers.description_en: Henri Turunen is a programme manager and executive producer at Oulu2026, working at the intersection of art, technology and cultural innovation within the European Capital of Culture programme.
Lowri Harries is Associate Curator of Canary Wharf’s Public Art programme, overseeing its permanent collection and temporary exhibitions, including the annual Winter Lights festival.
Kristian Horsburgh is Director of the 1535° Creative Hub in Differdange, where he develops an ecosystem dedicated to creative industries, cultural innovation and entrepreneurship in Luxembourg.

Adriano Martella is Head of Creative and Creative Director at Filmmaster, specialising in large-scale ceremonies, live shows and immersive experiences at the intersection of creativity and technology.

panels.title: Making It Real
panels.description_en:
Every large-scale artistic experience starts as a vision — and turning that vision into something audiences can actually walk into, feel, and remember is its own creative act. This panel brings together people who sit at that exact threshold: an agency that represents and produces for artists, executive production for ambitious creative projects, a studio building video content for global live entertainment, and a festival-studio hybrid navigating both sides at once.
Rather than treating production as the practical afterthought to the "real" creative work, this conversation explores how artistic decisions actually get made under pressure — what gets protected, what gets reinvented, and what a producer's eye brings to a project that a purely artistic one might miss.
Moderated by Claire Spencer Cook, whose own work sits at the intersection of immersive storytelling and production, the discussion moves between craft and constraint — asking what it really takes to turn an idea into an experience someone can step into.

Giulia De Paoli is a creative director and designer specialising in live experiences, stage design, lighting, real-time and generative content, and AI-driven visual workflows for large-scale events and performances.

speakers.role_en: Cofounder and Creative and Technical Director
speakers.description_en: Jean-Luc Gason is co-founder of Drop The Spoon, a Belgian creative studio specialising in video design, immersive content and architectural mapping for live shows and large-scale experiences.
Antonio J. Albertos is Director of Festival Volumens and Radiante Studio, working at the intersection of electronic music, audiovisual culture and digital creativity in Spain.

auto_fr.description:
Toute expérience artistique de grande envergure naît d’une vision — et transformer cette vision en quelque chose que les publics peuvent réellement parcourir, ressentir et garder en mémoire est un acte créatif à part entière. Cette table ronde réunit des personnes qui se trouvent précisément à cette croisée des chemins : une agence qui représente des artistes et produit leurs projets, la production exécutive de projets créatifs ambitieux, un studio qui crée des contenus vidéo pour des spectacles à travers le monde, et une structure hybride entre festival et studio qui navigue simultanément entre ces deux univers.
Plutôt que de considérer la production comme une simple étape pratique venant après le « vrai » travail créatif, cette conversation explore la manière dont les décisions artistiques se prennent réellement sous pression — ce que l’on préserve, ce que l’on réinvente, et ce que le regard d’un·e producteur·rice apporte à un projet et qu’un regard purement artistique pourrait laisser échapper.
Modérée par Claire Spencer Cook, dont le travail se situe à la croisée de la narration immersive et de la production, la discussion oscille entre savoir-faire et contraintes — pour interroger ce qu’il faut vraiment pour transformer une idée en une expérience dans laquelle on peut entrer.

panels.title: Coding Heritage
panels.description_en:
Technology doesn't stay in one lane — and neither does the question of what gets preserved, reinvented, or told in an entirely new way once it enters the picture. This panel brings together three very different technological approaches to the same tension: an independent studio using video games and AI to keep cultural heritage alive, an entrepreneur reinventing Belgium's own comic-strip heritage for the smartphone generation, and a festival platform showcasing the newest narrative forms across digital and mixed media.
Moderated by Ghita Amrati, whose own work as a director and screenwriter sits at the heart of shaping Morocco's digital art industry through storytelling, the conversation moves across mediums that rarely compare notes — asking what heritage, storytelling, and cultural memory actually mean once new technology reshapes the way they're told.

speakers.description_en: Antariksha Studio is an Indian transmedia collective blending video games, performance and digital art to create inclusive, futuristic narratives rooted in Indian culture, with a focus on Indofuturism, activism, pluralism and sustainability.

Elsewhere in India explores cultural heritage, digital technology and speculative futures through immersive and multidisciplinary formats, addressing decolonisation, digital repatriation and climate action from a Global South perspective.
David Mendlewicz is co-founder and CEO of Papegaai, an AI-native entertainment studio developing LUMIX, a vertical, animated and interactive storytelling format designed for mobile.

Diego Iglesias Gómez is a Spanish creative director, curator and educator, co-founder of MMMAD, HYPER HOUSE and HYPER STUDIO, working at the intersection of digital culture, contemporary art, design and technology.

auto_fr.description:

Cette table ronde réunit trois approches technologiques très différentes autour d’une même tension : un studio indépendant qui utilise les jeux vidéo et l’IA pour faire vivre le patrimoine culturel, un entrepreneur qui réinvente le patrimoine belge de la bande dessinée pour la génération smartphone, et une plateforme festivalière qui met en lumière les nouvelles formes narratives issues du numérique et des médias hybrides.
Animée par Ghita Amrati, dont le travail de réalisatrice et de scénariste contribue à façonner le secteur des arts numériques au Maroc à travers la narration, la conversation fait dialoguer des médiums qui échangent rarement entre eux — pour interroger ce que signifient réellement le patrimoine, la narration et la mémoire culturelle lorsque les nouvelles technologies transforment les façons de les raconter.

panels.title: Curating Under Constraint
panels.description_en:
Four curators, four completely different sets of constraints. From a major heritage institution balancing legacy and new technologies, to a hybrid music and digital art festival, to an independent platform bridging Europe and North Africa, to a homegrown music-tech scene building its own identity, this panel pulls back the curtain on how curatorial decisions actually get made, and what shapes them: budget, infrastructure, audience, or simply what's possible in a given context.

Moderated by Sarah Eve Tousignant, whose own experience navigating independent festival curation brings a sharp eye to the conversation, this is less a showcase of finished programmes than an honest look at process: the choices, the trade-offs, and the different definitions of what ""good curation"" even means.

moderator.description_en: Sarah Eve is a Montreal-based curator and cultural producer specialising in sound art, digital culture and DIY practices, with a focus on supporting interdisciplinary and socially engaged artistic projects.

speakers.description_en: Antònia Folguera is an independent curator with over 20 years of experience at the intersection of art, technology and digital culture, and is also active in radio and podcasting, notably with Eufònic, XRCB and Sónar+D.

speakers.description_en: Bettina Pelz is an internationally renowned curator specialising in light and media art, with over 25 years of experience developing interdisciplinary projects and light art festivals across Europe and Africa.

Jan Pauly is a Belgian project manager and consultant specialising in digital innovation, immersive technologies and the future of music and cultural experiences, particularly through his work with DAE Research at Howest.

Ginger Scott is Executive Director of InterAccess, bringing nearly 20 years of experience in arts administration, governance and non-profit cultural management across Canada, with a strong focus on artist-run and media arts organisations.

D’une grande institution patrimoniale qui conjugue héritage et nouvelles technologies à un festival hybride de musique et d’art numérique, d’une plateforme indépendante reliant l’Europe et l’Afrique du Nord à une scène locale mêlant musique et technologie qui construit sa propre identité, cette table ronde lève le voile sur la manière dont se prennent réellement les décisions de programmation et sur ce qui les façonne : le budget, les infrastructures, les publics, ou tout simplement ce qui est possible dans un contexte donné.

Animée par Sarah Eve Tousignant, dont l’expérience de la programmation de festivals indépendants apporte un regard aiguisé aux échanges, cette rencontre est moins une vitrine de programmes aboutis qu’un regard sincère sur les processus : les choix, les compromis et les différentes définitions de ce que signifie réellement un ""bon commissariat"".

panels.title: From Experiment to Ecosystem: Where Creativity, Research, Innovation & Technology Meet.
panels.description_en:
What happens when AI, immersive technologies, design, research and the arts come together? And what does it take to turn an exciting experiment into something that lasts? 

Switzerland offers an interesting perspective. Across its different linguistic regions and cantons, universities, creative professionals, technology companies and innovation networks are finding ways to work together. But collaboration is not always straightforward, and there is no single recipe for success. 

Bringing together six voices from across Switzerland, this panel explores how ideas move between research labs, creative studios, companies and innovation ecosystems. 

Through their experiences in AI, immersive technologies, digital fabrication, artistic research and innovation, the speakers will discuss what makes these collaborations possible, where the challenges lie and how promising experiments can grow into meaningful projects. 

An open conversation about connecting people, disciplines and ideas — and what we can learn from one another.

La Suisse offre une perspective intéressante. À travers ses différentes régions linguistiques et ses cantons, les universités, les professionnel·les de la création, les entreprises technologiques et les réseaux d’innovation trouvent des moyens de travailler ensemble. Mais la collaboration ne va pas toujours de soi, et il n’existe pas de recette unique pour réussir. 

Réunissant six voix venues de toute la Suisse, cette table ronde explore la circulation des idées entre laboratoires de recherche, studios de création, entreprises et écosystèmes d’innovation. 

À travers leurs expériences en IA, en technologies immersives, en fabrication numérique, en recherche artistique et en innovation, les intervenant·es discuteront de ce qui rend ces collaborations possibles, des défis qu’elles présentent et de la manière dont des expérimentations prometteuses peuvent devenir des projets porteurs de sens.

panels.title: Senses and Sensibility: When Immersion Looks Beyond Vision, presented by XN Québec
panels.description_en:
In 2026, immersion is no longer just about what audiences see. Studios and creators are discovering new ways to shape immersion and reach audiences, and technology now lets them go further than ever. It's not that we've seen it all in visual immersion. It's that we're discovering there's more to immersion than what meets the eye, literally. 

Could engaging senses beyond sight be a new way to deepen loyalty with existing audiences while opening the door to entirely new ones? The next step for immersive experiences and even a tool to make those productions even more accessible ? And what if the deepest immersion isn't something projected onto us, but something reflected back, our own body, made visible?

moderator.description_en: Sandra Felteau is Advisor for International Development and Partnerships at Xn Québec, where she fosters international collaborations, connects Quebec creative studios with global markets, and promotes Quebec talent across the international creative and technology ecosystem.

speakers.description_en: Marian Tremblay is an Executive Producer and Partner at mirari, bringing over 25 years of experience in digital arts, creative industries, production and organisational development to the studio’s immersive and multidisciplinary projects.

Marek Blottière is an R&D Project Manager at the Society for Arts and Technology (SAT) in Montréal, working on immersive technologies, open-source software, AI and the intersections between digital innovation and contemporary cultural practices.

Anouk Ethier is the creative force behind Noukii, a Montreal-based production company exploring the intersection of immersive experiences, artificial intelligence, digital technology and user-centred cultural experiences.

auto_fr.description:
En 2026, l’immersion ne se limite plus à ce que les publics voient. Les studios, créatrices et créateurs découvrent de nouvelles façons de façonner l’immersion et de toucher les publics, et la technologie leur permet désormais d’aller plus loin que jamais. Ce n’est pas que nous ayons tout vu en matière d’immersion visuelle. C’est que nous découvrons que l’immersion va au-delà de ce qui est visible, littéralement. 

Solliciter d’autres sens que la vue pourrait-il être une nouvelle façon de renforcer la fidélité des publics existants tout en ouvrant la porte à de tout nouveaux publics ? La prochaine étape pour les expériences immersives, voire un outil pour rendre ces productions encore plus accessibles ? Et si l’immersion la plus profonde n’était pas quelque chose que l’on projette sur nous, mais quelque chose qui nous est renvoyé en miroir : notre propre corps, rendu visible ?

panels.title: Water Resonances: Listening, Translating, Advocating
panels.description_en: Water teems with life, signals and patterns for us to dive in, decipher and care about. This panel brings together scientists studying aquatic life behavior, artists exploring water's flows and patterns, and advocates working to bring the importance of rivers, lakes and seas to human attention and decision-making systems.

moderator.description_en: Camilla Colombo is a curator whose practice explores the intersections between artistic enquiry and scientific research. With a background in the performing arts and in advocacy for the arts at the European level, she has worked in Italy, the UK, and Belgium, serving organisations of all sizes as well as independent artists, with a focus on multidisciplinary and multimedia productions. She has collaborated with and curated at contemporary art institutions in Belgium and abroad, such as BOZAR, iMAL, and LUMA Arles. She is co-founder and Artistic Director of Ohme (BE), an organisation investigating contemporary societal issues through transdisciplinary initiatives in arts and sciences.

speakers.description_en: Alex Jordan is an Australian marine biologist who leads the Behavioural Evolution Research Group at the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behaviour in Konstanz. He works underwater, in the oceans and lakes where fish live, and asks what their behaviour can and cannot tell us about their experience. He uses art as a bridge to the non-human world, and his collaborations with SUPERFLEX, Tomás Saraceno, Antoine Bertin and Ingo Niermann have been shown at the Venice Biennale, Desert X, The Shed and the UN Ocean Conference.

Paula Nishijima is a Brazilian visual artist whose research-based practice weaves together scientific perspectives, decolonial poetics, and nonhuman cosmologies. Her work explores the nonlinear temporalities and patterns of living systems – drawing connections to the human political and ethical dimensions. Her artistic research is materialized and documented through various media, such as video, games, art installations, and sculptures.

Hila considers natural pattern formations, fluid dynamics, and physical materials as programmable matter to be discovered, designed, and re-invented. At the core of Hila’s work is a vision of accessible creative tools for interactive materials that translate material dynamics into tangible human perception. Her work has been published in venues like ACM CHI and exhibited internationally. She holds a Master of Media Arts and Sciences from MIT Media Lab and a B.Des Cum Laude in Product Design from Bezalel Academy. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, she works towards accessible material interfaces that transform how we experience and interact with our daily environments.

Valentine Boccas is the Manager of cultural actions at the Tara Ocean foundation.  For more than twenty years, the Tara Ocean foundation has been conducting scientific expeditions around the world to study marine biodiversity and the impacts of climate change and pollution. Alongside its scientific research, Tara’s expeditions have encouraged collaboration with artists through the organization of more than 50 art-science residencies to help shape a new imaginary of the Ocean.

Elle est cofondatrice et directrice artistique d’Ohme (BE), une organisation qui étudie les enjeux sociétaux contemporains à travers des initiatives transdisciplinaires en arts et en sciences.

panels.title: Echoes from Below
panels.description_en: Underwater worlds reach us as echoes. Below the surface, they are known through images, recordings, data, stories and the imagined lives of aquatic beings. From these fragments we build, back on land, our relationship with the sea: one that can become care and protection, or convenient assumption and even indifference. These perceptions shape the policies, laws and decisions that govern how we relate to oceans, lakes and rivers. This panel brings together the perspectives of authors, artists, designers and policymakers to reflect on how these echoes are made, who shapes them, and how they travel from imagination to decision.

moderator.description_en: Filipa Ramos, PhD, is a writer and curator whose long-term research investigates art's relationship to ecology. She is particularly interested in animals and time-based media. Ramos teaches at the Art Institute at the FHNW Academy of Art and Design, Basel and is Curator of the 2027 edition of LIAF and co-curator of the 2028 Bergen Assembly. Together, with Lucia Pietroiusti she founded the arts, humanities and science festival "The Shape of a Circle in the Mind of a Fish" (2018-onwards). Recent projects include "BESTIARI," the Catalan representation at the 60th Venice Biennale (2024), "Songs for the Changing Seasons" for the 1. Klima Biennale Wien (2024) and in 2022, "Persons Personen," the 8th Biennale Gherdëina (both with Pietroiusti). In 2021, she co-curated "Bodies of Water," the 13th Shanghai Biennale. Her most recent book, "The Artist as Ecologist" (2025), discusses the ways in which contemporary artists embrace environmentalism.

speakers.company: Joint Research Center, EU Policy Lab
speakers.description_en: Elahe is a designer at the EU Policy lab. She designs tools, methods and processes for creative collaboration between the scientists and the policy makers. Before joining the EU commission, Elahe was the creative lead at the Open Innovation Centre of the University of Bologna. She led dozens of multidisciplinary and cross-generational teams in designing new product and services for various companies in pharma, food, automotive and entertainment industry. She was also a design educator and coach for student programs at the Design Factory Global Network and the Challenge Based Innovation at CERN IdeaSquare. She is passionate about Design in all its forms and functions and strives to bring speculative design and visual thinking into policymaking.

Ersin Han Ersin (b. 1984, Turkey) is an artist and director of Marshmallow Laser Feast, a London-based artist collective renowned for its pioneering experiential artworks. His practice spans sculpture, installation, live performance, merging art, ecology and technology to reveal the hidden natural forces that govern our shared Earth. Ersin’s works invite audiences to explore realms beyond ordinary perception, often stripping away the visible physical world to uncover interconnected networks, systems, and processes fundamental to life on Earth.

Tatiana Rosa and Pedro Matias create immersive, multisensory artworks exploring imperceptible ecologies and social phenomena. Tatiana foregrounds sound as agency, crafting experiences that reveal hidden materialities and invite a reconfiguration of how we listen and relate. Pedro, a transmaterial artist, investigates encounters across bodies, materials, and more-than-human worlds, blending poetry and politics in layered environments. Together, their collaborative practice transforms absence and silenced narratives into tangible, affective forms. Working across intermedia, performance, and installation, they merge critical reflection with sensory storytelling, inviting audiences into poetic, speculative engagements that challenge perception and cultivate new ways of sensing ecological and social realities.

panels.title: HIDROTOPIAS: Living with Changing Waters - Art, Communities & Ecological Adaptation
panels.description_en: Drawing on field research conducted in the Danube Delta, Hidrotopias explores how artistic practices can reveal the complex relationships between water, communities, other forms of life, and the infrastructures shaping aquatic environments.

moderator.description_en: Diane Pricop is an independent cultural producer who promotes artistic projects addressing the entanglement between environmental, social and technological challenges, through educational and interdisciplinary research practices.

speakers.description_en: Ioana Vreme Moser is a sound artist whose practice brings electronic circuits, repurposed components, and raw technological processes into dialogue with her own body and environmental stimuli, while reflecting on the history of technologies.

Floriama Cândea explores the relationships between objects, systems, and the ways we perceive them, by creating hybrid identities at the intersection of nature and technology, and by analysing the possibility of new forms of coexistence.

Through installations composed of objects, light, and sound, Pepa Ivanova investigates the interconnected factors that contribute to the adaptation and transformation of ecosystems, as well as relationships between species.

panels.title: Beyond Stereo: The Rise of Immersive Sound
panels.description_en:
For decades, live music has largely been built around the same idea: a stage in front of an audience, with sound projected towards them. Spatial audio is beginning to challenge that model.

Immersive stages are appearing at festivals, clubs are being designed around 360° sound systems, dedicated listening rooms are turning album playback into a collective experience, and artists and sound designers are increasingly treating sound as a space audiences can physically enter.

Rather than simply coming from the stage, music can now move above, behind and around the listener, transforming sound into a powerful tool for storytelling, emotion, presence and experience design.

But what does this shift mean for the future of live entertainment? How does spatial sound change the relationship between artists and audiences? What new creative possibilities emerge when musicians, venues, engineers and experience designers start thinking beyond stereo from the very beginning? And can immersive sound move from spectacular one-off experiences to become a new standard for live music and entertainment?

Bringing together perspectives from Polygon Productions, Club Wintercircus, AREAL Technologies and Delacroix Studio, alongside audio research, this panel explores the rapidly evolving ecosystem of immersive sound, from festivals and clubs to listening spaces, experiential installations, new technologies and entirely new ways of experiencing music.

moderator.description_en: Brecht De Man is an audio researcher, educator and engineer working at the intersection of music, technology and sound. As Head of Research at PXL-Music and President of the international Audio Engineering Society, he brings together research, industry and creative practice to explore what new audio technologies mean for artists, venues and audiences.

speakers.description_en: Nico Elliott is co-founder and CEO of Polygon Productions, the team behind Polygon Live and Polygon Portal in London. Polygon creates music experiences built around 360° spatial audio, from large-scale festival environments to intimate listening spaces where audiences are placed inside the music.

Wouter Vanhaelemeesch is part of the team behind Club Wintercircus, the underground music venue inside Ghent’s spectacular Wintercircus. Designed as a 360° environment for concerts, nightlife and audiovisual experimentation, the club explores new formats for spatial audio concerts, immersive listening sessions and live audiovisual experiences.

Kristof Jeuris is Commercial Director at AREAL Technologies, a company developing innovative spatial audio solutions for live entertainment, music venues and immersive experiences. Working at the intersection of audio technology and the live industry, he helps bring immersive sound into real-world environments, including Club Wintercircus in Ghent. His perspective focuses on how spatial audio technologies can become accessible, scalable tools for creating new ways of experiencing music and live entertainment.

Laurent Dupuy is a Grammy Award-winning mixing engineer and co-founder and CTO of Delacroix Studio, an immersive audio agency creating spatial sound experiences across culture, entertainment and experiential design. His work explores how immersive audio can move beyond technology to become a creative medium for storytelling, emotion and audience engagement.

Depuis des décennies, la musique live repose largement sur la même idée : une scène face à un public, vers lequel le son est projeté. L’audio spatial commence à remettre ce modèle en question.

Des scènes immersives font leur apparition dans les festivals, des clubs sont conçus autour de systèmes sonores à 360°, des salles d’écoute dédiées transforment la diffusion d’albums en expérience collective, et les artistes et les spécialistes de la création sonore envisagent de plus en plus le son comme un espace dans lequel le public peut physiquement entrer.

Plutôt que de simplement provenir de la scène, la musique peut désormais se déplacer au-dessus, derrière et autour des personnes qui l’écoutent, faisant du son un puissant outil de narration, d’émotion, de présence et de conception d’expériences.

Mais que signifie cette évolution pour l’avenir du spectacle vivant ? Comment le son spatial transforme-t-il la relation entre les artistes et les publics ? Quelles nouvelles possibilités créatives émergent lorsque musicien·nes, lieux de diffusion, ingénieur·es et concepteur·ices d’expériences pensent au-delà de la stéréo dès le départ ? Et le son immersif peut-il dépasser le stade des expériences ponctuelles spectaculaires pour devenir une nouvelle norme dans la musique live et le spectacle vivant ?

En croisant les perspectives de Polygon Productions, Club Wintercircus, AREAL Technologies et Delacroix Studio avec celles de la recherche audio, cette table ronde explore l’écosystème en pleine évolution du son immersif : des festivals et clubs aux espaces d’écoute, en passant par les installations expérientielles, les nouvelles technologies et des manières entièrement nouvelles de vivre la musique.

panels.title: Play Testing Digital Transformation
panels.description:
Comment les artistes peuvent repenser notre manière d’apprendre la technologie

L’éducation numérique se concentre souvent sur l’apprentissage de l’utilisation des technologies. Mais si les artistes pouvaient nous aider à apprendre à les questionner, à les détourner, à les démonter et à les imaginer autrement ?

À travers Play Test!, KIKK, NODE Forum et Creative Coding Utrecht ont expérimenté une approche différente de l’éducation numérique : réunir des artistes, des enseignant·es et des animateur·rices jeunesse afin de développer de nouvelles façons de sensibiliser les jeunes à la technologie.

Du creative coding et de l’électronique DIY aux pratiques low-tech, au réemploi et au permacomputing, le projet envisage la pratique artistique non pas simplement comme un moyen de rendre la technologie plus attrayante, mais comme un outil d’apprentissage par l’expérimentation, la pensée critique et le jeu. Play Test! a été conçu autour de trois workshops organisés en Belgique, en Allemagne et aux Pays-Bas, avec des méthodologies pensées pour être transmises aux animateur·rices jeunesse et, à terme, aux jeunes eux-mêmes.

Lors de cette discussion, Jeanne Charlotte Vogt (NODE), Melissa Van Der Lingen (CCU), Charlotte Benedetti (KIKK / Le Pavillon) et l’artiste Marie Verdeil partageront leurs expériences autour de Play Test! et d’autres projets afin d’explorer une question plus large : les artistes peuvent-ils devenir un chaînon manquant entre la transformation technologique et l’éducation ?
panels.description_en:
How artists can reshape the way we learn about technology

Digital education often focuses on learning how to use technology. But what if artists could help us learn how to question it, hack it, take it apart and imagine it differently?

Through Play Test!, KIKK, NODE Forum and Creative Coding Utrecht have been experimenting with a different approach to digital education: bringing artists, educators and youth workers together to develop new ways of engaging young people with technology.

From creative coding and DIY electronics to low-tech practices, reuse and permacomputing, the project considers artistic practice not simply as a way of making technology more attractive, but as a tool for learning through experimentation, critical thinking and play. Play Test! was conceived around three workshops in Belgium, Germany and the Netherlands, with methodologies designed to be transferable to youth workers and ultimately to young people.


For this conversation, Jeanne Charlotte Vogt (NODE), Melissa Van Der Lingen [CCU], Charlotte Benedetti (KIKK / Le Pavillon) and artist Marie Verdeil will share experiences from Play Test! and other projects to explore a broader question: can artists become a missing link between technological transformation and education?

panels.title: PITCH SESSIONS - Vanna, Cercle des créateurs digitaux, United XR & OKUS Lab

speakers.description_en: How can we break isolation and bring purpose back to our practices? We’re opening up the behind-the-scenes of building Vanna, a multidisciplinary creative hub designed to reconnect the creative sector. Faced with industry anxiety about the future, creating authentic spaces to gather is essential for having unfiltered conversations, sharing vulnerabilities, and reintroducing play into how we collaborate. Join us for an immersive session where we will also present our latest creative sandbox, an emotional barometer designed to map and discuss mental well-being in the creative industry, as well as a preview of our upcoming trainings, workshops, and performances.

OKUS LAB is a Belgian creative studio founded by choreographer and transmedia visual artist Emmanuel Di Martino, exploring the intersection of dance, light, visual arts and immersive technologies. Through projects such as OKUS PENDULUM, OKUS PAPYRUS and FOKUS Immersive, the studio develops hybrid experiences that connect the human body, light, moving images and space. Blending live performance, digital scenography, video mapping and extended reality (VR/AR), OKUS LAB creates new ways of experiencing movement, perception and visual storytelling. Its work is designed to engage with performing arts, museums, heritage spaces and innovative cultural environments, opening up new possibilities for artistic expression and collaboration across disciplines.

panels.title: Creative industries: business as unusual
panels.description: De la valorisation multi-canale d'IP à la monétisation de contenus auprès des communautés de fans, des mécanismes de financement public–privé au “pay per experience”, aux systèmes de licences, la nature même de la création digitale et des industries créatives mettent au défi les modes classiques de financement de projets et les business models “as usual”. Plusieurs experts du financement, des solutions et des modèles d'affaires de l'économie créative en Belgique et au Luxembourg se rencontrent pour tracer un périmètre des enjeux pour nos créateurs entre défis et opportunités, et partager des expériences gagnantes et inspirantes.
panels.description_en:
From the multi-channel exploitation of IP to the monetization of content among fan communities, from public-private funding mechanisms to “pay-per-experience” models and licensing systems, the very nature of digital creation and the creative industries challenges traditional project financing methods and conventional business models.

Several experts in financing, solutions and business models within the creative economy in Belgium and Luxembourg are coming together to explore the challenges and opportunities facing creators, while sharing successful and inspiring experiences.

speakers.description_en:
FOKUS IMMERSIVE is a digital ballet project exploring choreographic mutation, inspired by genetic mutation. Just as mutations transform living organisms, the project investigates how movement can evolve and generate new choreographic forms through digital technologies.

Created by Belgian choreographer and transmedia artist Emmanuel Di Martino / OKUS LAB, it brings together dance, science and immersive technologies through virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR).

This presentation focuses on the AR prototype, developed in collaboration with developer Anthony Bayet and demonstrated on Android devices. By integrating digital choreography into the viewer’s physical environment, FOKUS IMMERSIVE explores new ways of experiencing dance beyond the stage.

Currently in development, the project aims to expand the boundaries of choreography through immersive experiences, connecting biological transformation, artistic creation and technological innovation.

At DeepMedia, we built our own brain: Hermes. He thinks like you.

Hermes is not the writer. It is DeepMedia’s cognitive layer: it remembers the lessons learned with a customer, thinks before generating content, can block outputs that violate its guardrails, and injects his cognitive brief into the generation process. The more you publish, the more it learns.

Same AI model. Different judgment. Because the memory and reasoning are shaped by the client’s own experience and editorial standards.

Most AI tools forget everything as soon as the conversation ends.
They start from scratch with every new piece of content.

Hermes, on the other hand, builds an institutional editorial memory: past feedback, lessons learned, daily briefings, and bias signals.

Whenever new content is requested, that memory comes back into play — like an experienced editor saying: “We've seen this trap before. Watch out.”

The result? Fewer repeated mistakes, greater consistency over time, and AI-generated content that is no longer just generally intelligent, but informed by the organization's own experience.
